stories.title: Progressives grow sway in Lansing, push to tax the rich and corporations
stories.summary: Incoming House Speaker Ranjeev Puri of Canton will navigate a Michigan Legislature with a growing progressive caucus in 2027. This group aims to push for policies like increased corporate income tax, government ethics reforms, and potentially a state-level single-payer healthcare system, though the latter faces leadership resistance. Puri will need to balance these ambitions with the broader caucus's agenda.

inputFacts.title: Progressives grow sway in Lansing, push to tax the rich and corporations

While party leadership remains focused on broader affordability goals, these lawmakers aim to leverage their increased numbers to push for more ambitious, anti-corporate policy changes.

stories.title: Ann Arbor-born artist jazz Stratøs stops by the WEMU studio
stories.summary: Ann Arbor-born jazz artist Stratøs, a three-time Herb Alpert Young Jazz Composer Award winner, discussed his new album "Challenger Deep" and its themes rooted in his Barbadian heritage and family history. He also reflected on his musical upbringing in Ann Arbor and Detroit, including his time with the Detroit Symphony Orchestra's youth programs.

stories.title: U-M addiction specialist warns of kratom health risks
stories.summary: A University of Michigan addiction specialist warns that kratom products, particularly those containing synthetic opioids like 7-OH, can affect the brain similarly to fentanyl and heroin, leading to addiction. Plymouth Township has enacted its own restrictions on kratom sales, while statewide legislation remains stalled.

inputFacts.title: U-M addiction specialist warns of kratom health risks
inputFacts.summary: As Michigan House Bill 5537 remains stalled in the state Senate, some local communities are enacting their own bans on kratom sales. University of Michigan addiction specialist Eliza Hutchinson warns that synthetic opioids found in these products can lead to rapid addiction and pose significant health risks.

editorial.reason: The article discusses health risks associated with kratom, a substance that has prompted local civic action in Plymouth Township, a community directly adjacent to Canton. The stalled state legislation and local responses make this a relevant local issue.

stories.title: Ypsi Township to hold panel discussion at EMU on U-M/Los Alamos project
stories.summary: Ypsilanti Township will host a panel discussion at Eastern Michigan University regarding the proposed University of Michigan/Los Alamos National Laboratory computing research center. The discussion will include the executive director of Nuclear Watch New Mexico, who has expressed concerns about the partnership's implications for AI and nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Zoning can make or break small business success
stories.summary: Dexter's evolving zoning ordinances, including changes for mixed-use development and outdoor dining, have supported its local economy and small businesses. Experts suggest that municipalities should review zoning to reduce barriers for entrepreneurs, as complex regulations can hinder business establishment and growth, impacting local vitality.

inputFacts.title: Zoning can make or break small business success
inputFacts.summary: The City of Dexter has utilized strategic zoning updates over the past 50 years to foster a thriving historic downtown and commercial corridor. Experts note that flexible, form-based codes and streamlined permitting processes are essential tools for supporting small business growth and economic development.

inputFacts.summary: As International Survivors of Suicide Loss Day approaches on November 21st, experts highlight the significant impact of suicide on veteran communities and the importance of postvention support. inputFacts.title: Federal judge considers rare review of grand jury proceedings in U-M protest case
inputFacts.summary: A federal judge is considering an unusual request to review grand jury testimony in the case of Zainab Hakim, one of 12 individuals charged in connection with pro-Palestinian protests. The defense argues that prosecutors may have presented misleading information regarding an alleged evidence-tampering incident involving a laptop during an FBI raid. The judge has adjourned the bail hearing until December 2 to research legal precedents for unsealing grand jury proceedings.

inputFacts.title: Brighton’s Holiday Glow & Market
inputFacts.summary: Brighton’s Holiday Glow & Market is a downtown holiday kickoff event featuring local vendors, family activities, and live reindeer. The celebration includes live performances, a train, and a tree lighting ceremony with Santa and Mrs. Claus.

inputFacts.title: Riverside’s 2026 Holiday Art Fair
inputFacts.summary: Riverside Arts Center in Ypsilanti is hosting a holiday art fair featuring over 60 local artisans. The event includes handmade art, vintage goods, self-care products, food, and mini golf.

inputFacts.title: Tyree Guyton at The Shepherd
inputFacts.summary: An exhibition of gallery work by artist Tyree Guyton is on view at The Shepherd in Detroit through November 21. The article reflects on the history of the Heidelberg Project and Guyton's artistic legacy in the city.

inputFacts.title: Detroit Metro Airport opens new North Cell Phone Lot
inputFacts.summary: Detroit Metro Airport has opened a new North Cell Phone Lot at Rogell and Burton Drive to provide a more convenient location for passenger pickups. With the opening, airport officials are strictly enforcing a ban on parking in front of the Evans and McNamara Terminals, with violators subject to fines and towing.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor drivers are failing to use turn signals, placing cyclists under threat
inputFacts.summary: Despite receiving a gold-level Bicycle Friendly Community award in 2022, Ann Arbor continues to see a high average of vehicle-bicycle accidents. The report highlights ongoing safety concerns for cyclists due to driver negligence, specifically the failure to use turn signals.

inputFacts.title: Expect University of Michigan's next athletic director to clean house, John U. Bacon says
inputFacts.summary: John U. Bacon discusses potential changes within the University of Michigan football program and the future of the athletic department. The segment also touches on the Detroit Lions' defense following Aidan Hutchinson's injury.

inputFacts.title: The Eastern Harvest tackles food insecurity through community partnerships
inputFacts.summary: A partnership between Eastern Michigan University and Chartwells Dining Services, known as The Eastern Harvest, is working to address year-round food insecurity for families in Washtenaw County.

inputFacts.title: U-M Board of Regents votes to proceed with Ypsi Township research computing center
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan Board of Regents has officially voted to move forward with construction plans for a new research computing center located in Ypsilanti Township.
